title: TripleSumm: Adaptive Triple-Modality Fusion for Video Summarization
encoders: MoSu: CLIP ViT-L/14, RoBERTa-base, AST; external datasets use existing visual features plus generated captions/audio.
sampling: MoSu: 1 visual/text/audio feature per second; audio uses centered 10-second windows.
architecture: Alternating temporal and cross-modal blocks; D=128; sigmoid score head (Appendix A.1).
fusion: Per-frame fusion tokens combine visual, text and audio; temporal windows grow 5,15,45,N.
objective: Section 3.3 Eq. (7): L = ||S - S_hat||_2^2 against importance targets; no reconstruction objective.
training_data: MoSu replay-derived targets; separately target-dataset supervision or MoSu pretraining then target fine-tuning.
test_data: MoSu; Mr. HiSum; SumMe; TVSum; separate 50-video long-form set.
split: MoSu: 42,152 train / 5,263 validation / 5,263 test. SumMe/TVSum: TV 5-fold (4 train,1 evaluation) versus TVT (3 train,1 validation,1 test), Appendix B.5.
budget: 15% duration for keyshots (Appendix A.2); mAP uses a distinct segment-ranking protocol.
postprocessing: KTS, mean shot score, 0/1 knapsack; not applied to raw-score rank correlations.
weights: Official MoSu and Mr. HiSum checkpoints at https://huggingface.co/smkim37/TripleSumm (MIT); not executed.
features: MoSu card: https://huggingface.co/datasets/hminjeong/TripleSumm-MoSu; three (N,768) feature arrays per video, metadata, GT and split files; CC-BY-4.0.
reproducibility: Primary-source and repository inspection only; no model was executed; commit/release pin not independently verified.
limitations: Supervised/weak target regression; zero-shot denotes MoSu-to-long-video transfer only. Main Table 2 and Appendix Table XI agree, but Appendix D prose gives different MoSu rank values. External-dataset captioner is Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct in Section 5.1 versus the Qwen/Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct link in Appendix B.4; resolve model/cache provenance. Missing-modality and feature-extraction costs must be tracked.

title: VideoXum: Cross-modal Visual and Textural Summarization of Videos
encoders: BLIP visual encoder and pretrained text decoder; VTSUM-BLIP baseline.
sampling: 1 frame per second in VideoXum representation.
architecture: Shared video representation feeds frame-importance and text-generation decoders.
fusion: Shared visual encoding supports jointly aligned visual and text outputs.
objective: Section IV-B Eqs. (6)-(7): frame binary cross-entropy plus autoregressive text negative log likelihood; overall multitask objective Section IV-C.
training_data: VideoXum human summary annotations derived from ActivityNet Captions.
budget: Paper: intended top 15% of frames. Inspected F1 helper keeps scores >= the zero-based threshold at floor(0.15*N), selecting floor(0.15*N)+1 frames with distinct scores and possibly more with ties.
postprocessing: Frame threshold selection, not KTS keyshots. F1 is computed for each human mask and aggregated; the rank-metric path compares scores with the mean of ten masks. VT-CLIPScore uses a separate top-k path.
weights: Official model zoo on Hugging Face linked by repository.
features: Author-provided annotations and model/feature preparation instructions.
reproducibility: Primary paper and selected source inspected at commit 11bd4fe3fb51b7dc804dd1519a4914f67bff60df; no model execution or independent result reproduction.
limitations: Repository badge uses TMM 2023; archival volume is 2024. Released F1 threshold can exceed the intended 15% frame budget. F1 reference averaging and correlation against the mean reference are distinct; neither is the classic KTS keyshot protocol.

title: Align and Attend: Multimodal Summarization with Dual Contrastive Losses
encoders: GoogLeNet visual features on SumMe/TVSum; RoBERTa text features; dataset-specific encoders detailed in Appendix B.
sampling: Time-stamped video frames and transcript sentences; dataset-dependent sampling.
architecture: Multimodal Transformer, modality experts and two importance heads.
fusion: Shared segment positional embeddings and alignment-guided self-attention exploit transcript/frame timing.
objective: Section 3.4: modality focal classification losses plus inter-sample and intra-sample contrastive terms. Intra-sample positives use ground-truth summaries.
training_data: Annotated SumMe/TVSum, Daily Mail/CNN, BLiSS in separate experiments.
test_data: SumMe; TVSum; Daily Mail; CNN; BLiSS.
split: Dataset-specific splits and standard-video splits in Appendix B; exact split artifacts not independently verified.
budget: Dataset-dependent; exact configuration not independently verified.
weights: Official README links checkpoint archive on Google Drive; archive contents not downloaded.
features: Author feature archive; BLiSS raw-video URLs require contacting authors per README.
reproducibility: Primary-source and repository inspection only; no model was executed; commit/release pin not independently verified.
limitations: Contrastive losses do not make this label-free: classification and within-example contrast require annotated summaries. BLiSS livestream source does not establish causal online processing.

title: Scaling Up Video Summarization Pretraining with Large Language Models
encoders: CLIP ViT-L/14; SRoBERTa-NLI-large; Whisper for source transcripts.
architecture: 6-layer visual encoder, 3-layer text encoder, cross-attention and 6-layer summary decoder.
fusion: Visual queries attend to transcript keys/values; text masking permits visual-only inference.
objective: Section 4.1 Eq. (10): sum_i ||y_hat_i-y_i||^2 including EOS; target is an LLM-derived pseudo-summary, not reconstruction of the full input.
training_data: LfVS-P from filtered HowTo100M; timestamp-preserving LLM summaries; target fine-tuning treated separately.
test_data: LfVS-T (1,200 professionally annotated videos); SumMe; TVSum.
split: LfVS-P pretraining and separate LfVS-T test; classical target-data settings must remain separate.
budget: Autoregressive EOS termination; exact external benchmark budget not independently verified.
postprocessing: Nearest-neighbor matching of decoded features to input CLIP features, then temporal aggregation.
reproducibility: Primary-source and repository inspection only; no model was executed; commit/release pin not independently verified.
limitations: Depends on speech/visual alignment and teacher-summary quality; pseudo labels constitute external supervision. Public official release not located in inspected primary sources.

title: V2Xum-LLM: Cross-Modal Video Summarization with Temporal Prompt Instruction Tuning
architecture: Frozen visual encoder, trainable adapter and language decoder.
fusion: Interleave visual tokens with textual frame-index prompts; task instruction controls output modality.
objective: Training Eq. (4): autoregressive negative log likelihood over output visual-index/text tokens; adapter and language decoder updated.
training_data: LCS-558K adapter pretraining; VideoXum/Instruct-V2Xum summarization training; 30,000-video Instruct-V2Xum uses machine-assisted annotation.
split: Dataset-specific task splits; exact split-file identities not independently verified.
budget: Task-dependent generated frame indices; exact decoding/budget configuration not independently verified.
postprocessing: Temporal-index parsing; Appendix derives importance from language-model logits.
features: Dataset and model links available through official project.
reproducibility: Primary-source and repository inspection only; no model was executed; commit/release pin not independently verified.
limitations: Fine-tuned summarizer, not zero-shot; semantic CLIP metrics are not temporal-overlap F1. Initial arXiv 2024; AAAI publication 2025; inspected v3 updated October 2025.

title: Video Summarization with Large Language Models
sampling: Caption/frame timeline; exact frame-sampling configuration not independently verified.
architecture: LLM query/answer embeddings feed dimension reduction and 3 self-attention blocks.
fusion: Language bottleneck: frame captions to local windows, then global self-attention.
objective: Section 3.5 Eq. (6): mean_t (s_t-s_hat_t)^2 against human frame-importance targets.
training_data: SumMe/TVSum; example captions sampled from SumMe training set for in-context prompts.
test_data: SumMe; TVSum; separate Mr. HiSum zero-shot ablation.
split: Five dataset splits; validation/test independence not established by this audit.
budget: Standard short-video budget configuration not independently verified.
postprocessing: KTS and shot aggregation (Section 4.2); primary results emphasize rank metrics.
weights: Official README links model checkpoints for dataset splits.
features: Repository documents captions/LLM embeddings and data download.
reproducibility: Primary-source and repository inspection only; no model was executed; commit/release pin not independently verified.
limitations: Frozen LLM components do not make the global aggregator training-free. Paper reports 5 A100 GPUs; caption errors and context-window choices affect results.

title: Prompts to Summaries: Zero-Shot Language-Guided Video Summarization with Large Language and Video Models
encoders: CLIP ViT-L/14 embeddings; LLaVA/Qwen video captioner; GPT-family scene judge (model ablations).
sampling: Appendix A.5: 1 fps full video, 2 fps scenes, batches of 80; Section 3.2 also describes 1 fps scene processing, requiring implementation check.
architecture: Scene detection, scene/global captioning, LLM scene judgment and frame score propagation.
fusion: Prompt combines scene, global description and optional user query.
objective: No gradient objective; Sections 3.3-3.4 define prompted scene scoring, normalization, temporal smoothing and consistency/uniqueness frame weighting.
training_data: No selector training; pretrained models. Normalization selected with dataset experiments.
split: No learned selector splits; independence of calibration experiments not established.
budget: 15% for SumMe/TVSum; 36% for VidSum-Reason, with 3% fragments.
postprocessing: Scene/frame weighting and temporal-overlap evaluation; exact subset solver not independently verified.
weights: Off-the-shelf foundation checkpoints; no task-trained selector checkpoint.
features: Repository includes benchmark directories and VidSum-Reason resources.
reproducibility: Primary-source and repository inspection only; no model was executed; commit/release pin not independently verified.
limitations: Dataset-dependent Min-Max/Exponential normalization; held-out calibration unresolved. README clone command names an older repository. API/model versions and caption-cache provenance required.

title: SD-VSum: A Method and Dataset for Script-Driven Video Summarization
encoders: Frozen VideoXum-finetuned CLIP visual/text encoders; 512-dimensional features.
architecture: 8-head cross-modal attention, Transformer frame scorer and sigmoid head.
fusion: Video frames align with sentence embeddings from the desired-summary script.
objective: Section 4.2: BCE against the matching annotator summary for script-driven task; MSE against average annotator scores for generic variant.
training_data: S-VideoXum: 10 human summaries/video paired with LLaVA-NeXT-Video-generated scripts.
split: VideoXum train/validation/test partition; each script pairs with its own reference. S-NewsVSum uses 5-fold CV.
postprocessing: Frame ranking; average F1 across script-reference pairs, then videos; not best-reference matching.
weights: Official README links pretrained SD-VSum checkpoint.
features: Zenodo S-VideoXum release includes CLIP H5 features, labels, split JSON and scripts.
reproducibility: Primary-source and repository inspection only; no model was executed; commit/release pin not independently verified.
limitations: Machine-generated scripts may encode target-summary artifacts. Generic and script-conditioned losses/references differ; keep results separate.

title: Context-Aware Pseudo-Label Scoring for Zero-Shot Video Summarization
encoders: Video-language captioner and GPT-5 judge; exact pinned captioner not independently verified.
sampling: Scene detector and temporally sampled caption inputs; exact rate not independently verified.
architecture: Scene division, captioning, labeled reason/rubric construction, prompted scoring, temporal smoothing.
fusion: Scene captions plus neighboring/global captions condition a dataset-specific rubric.
objective: No gradient objective; Section 3 uses human-annotated examples to create pseudo scores and rubrics; Section 3.4 defines rubric scoring.
training_data: Small human-annotated subset for rubric construction; no gradient training claimed.
split: Disjointness of rubric-construction examples from evaluation videos not independently verified.
postprocessing: Scene-to-frame temporal smoothing and dataset-specific evaluation scripts.
features: Scripts and prompt/rubric files released; data paths require preparation.
reproducibility: Primary-source and repository inspection only; no model was executed; commit/release pin not independently verified.
limitations: The title says zero-shot but rubric construction uses labels; classify as label-assisted calibration. Draft contains placeholder conference/DOI metadata and inaccurate baseline attributions; exclude numerical comparisons pending protocol audit.

title: Cut to the Chase: Training-free Multimodal Summarization via Chain-of-Events
encoders: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct default; Whisper for missing transcripts; proprietary LLM calls where configured.
sampling: Up to 72 uniformly sampled frames, initially 12 clips; up to 30 frames per merged clip.
architecture: Hierarchical Event Graph, spatial grounding, event-evolution reasoning, domain-adaptive summary generation.
fusion: Explicit alignment of textual events/entities to visual evidence and temporal transitions.
objective: No gradient loss; Section 3 builds and reasons over event graphs; Section 3.5 uses example-guided style adaptation.
training_data: No gradient training; Section 4.1 samples five training-set summaries as style references.
test_data: VIEWS; MM-AVS; XMSMO-News; TIB; VISTA; BLiSS; SoccerNet-Caption; SummScreen3D.
split: Dataset test sets with training-set style exemplars; exemplar identity not independently verified.
budget: Text-generation length/configuration; no 15% extractive duration budget.
postprocessing: Event-centric generation and style adaptation, then text metrics.
framework: Python 3.12, PyTorch, vLLM; MongoDB-backed data preparation.
weights: Off-the-shelf Qwen model; no task-trained checkpoint.
features: Graph construction and evaluation scripts; underlying dataset access/preparation required.
reproducibility: Primary-source and repository inspection only; no model was executed; commit/release pin not independently verified.
limitations: Text-only output cannot be ranked with keyshot F1. Training-free does not mean no labeled examples: five reference summaries supply style. Judge versions and paid API components affect reproducibility.

title: EdgeVidSum: Real-Time Personalized Video Summarization at the Edge
venue: CVPR 2025 Demo; arXiv report (not a main-track benchmark paper)
encoders: ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNetV2 backbone; exact base/S variant inconsistent between report and poster.
sampling: Pre-generated thumbnail containers representing the whole video; density not reported.
architecture: EfficientNetV2, triplet attention, dense layers and softmax activity classifier.
fusion: Visual thumbnail activity predictions intersect with user preferences.
objective: Section 3.2.2: end-to-end cross-entropy for activity classification.
test_data: Demo movies, sports and documentaries; benchmark manifest not reported.
budget: Variable playback rates; no fixed keyshot compression budget reported.
postprocessing: Preferred-content timestamps guide adaptive fast-forward playback.
framework: Jetson Nano deployment; software framework not reported.
features: Requires service-provider thumbnail containers; public feature archive not verified.
reproducibility: Primary-source and repository inspection only; no model was executed; commit/release pin not independently verified.
limitations: Fast interaction on precomputed thumbnails is not causal online summarization; preprocessing/network costs and training protocol are incompletely reported. No public author code located.
